The disputed adversarial finding at EventReplicationInbox.cs:174 is upheld: a project\\u0027s id is minted per install (ProjectAddCommand, and MessageStreamId, MessageInbox, and MessageSweepEngine all state that the local project id differs per install for the identical shared project), so a replicated TaskAdded applied with the sender\\u0027s ProjectId lands under a project this node does not have and never shows in its own project\\u0027s views. The fix session\\u0027s exclusion of the whole Project stream is also not acceptable as it stands: criterion 1 makes the team part of project settings project-scoped, and the objective says every project-scoped event travels, so ProjectTeamSettingsChanged must reach teammates. The design to apply, which is the codebase\\u0027s existing precedent that the shared identity of a project is its ledger repository and the local id is a coordinate: (1) the inbox already receives the local project id it is reading for (ReadFromAsync\\u0027s projectId parameter, passed by MessageSweepEngine per project), so on apply every replicated event\\u0027s project coordinate is rewritten to that local id: Task, Idea, Epic, and Run events that carry a ProjectId field get the local id in the applied copy, with the sender\\u0027s original project id kept in the origin headers beside origin owner, node, event id, and sequence; (2) the Project aggregate\\u0027s project-scoped events (the team part, ProjectTeamSettingsChanged, and any other project-scoped event on that stream) are applied to this node\\u0027s own Project stream id instead of the sender\\u0027s, while node-part settings and the identity events (ProjectRegistered and its namespace siblings) stay excluded exactly as IsProjectStreamItself and the inbox scope check do now; (3) the outbox\\u0027s origin headers carry the sender\\u0027s project id so a forwarded copy (M2b) can be rewritten again at each hop, and dedupe stays by origin event id. Tests through the seam: two stores registered under DIFFERENT project ids exchange a task\\u0027s events and each reaches the same projection under its own project id; a team settings change on one store applies to the other store\\u0027s own Project stream and the node part does not travel; the existing same-id tests keep passing. Record the rule in the branch\\u0027s Decisions Log entry and the CLI reference in one sentence each: the project id is a local coordinate rewritten on apply, the ledger repository is the shared identity. Everything else in the fix position stands as fixed; do not reopen it. Leave no conflict marker; build and the scoped tests must pass before you
